confirmed.title: Gmail compose at 200% zoom or 400 px: Escape or Sift's Close hides the draft only in Sift, and there is then no way back to it (F700 leftover)
confirmed.where: http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/gmail.html at a 640x450 CSS px viewport (1280x900 at 200%) or 400x800
confirmed.evidence: Tested at 640x450, scale 2. Compose opens as a modal sheet 'New Message' (aria-modal=true, main.inert=true). After typing 'a@b' and pressing Escape: Sift has no dialog and no draft, while the page's compose is still open with To 'a@b'. Opening 'Your package was delivered' and then Back to Inbox: Sift's text still has no 'a@b' and shows no draft. Clicking Compose again gives an empty sheet, and the page's To becomes '' (the draft is lost on this fixture). At 400x800 the first three steps give the same result. On the original page at the same size, Escape and clicks elsewhere leave the draft open and visible. At 1280x900 the draft is an inline form and all of this works (see F700 recheck). With a page close control (r7dlg8-gmail-saveclose.html?es=1), Escape runs 'Guardar y cerrar' and the page saves the draft, so the problem needs a compose box with no close control. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/t5r8-f700-z200-open.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/t5r8-f700-z200-after.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5/research/shots/t5r8-f700-z200-compose-again.png
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-5 && SIFT_PORT=9465 ./scripts/chrome.sh start && SIFT_PORT=9465 SIFT_TAB=x bun research/r8t5/f700-zoom.ts 640 450 2   (prints 'Escape: siftDialog:null, siftTo:null, pageTo:a@b', then 'back: ... Sift text has a@b: false', then 'Compose: siftTo:"", pageTo:""'). Same with arguments 400 800 1. Control: 1280 900 1 gives an inline form (siftDialog:null, inert false).
confirmed.suspectedCause: floatingCompose() in src/content/adapters/gmail.ts treats a compose box as floating only when its area is under 50% of the viewport. At 640x450 the 500x400 box is 69%, so composeDialog() makes it page.dialog. Its dismissal now persists, because the ref was added. The box has no close control to replay, so Sift hides it and keeps it hidden while the page still shows it. A lead: never let Escape or Close dismiss a compose dialog that has no close of its own (render it as the inline form instead), or base 'floating' on the absence of a backdrop rather than on area.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, but this is the same defect as the F700 recheck (the reporter calls it the F700 leftover). Merge it into F700 rather than giving it a new id. At 640x450 scale 2 (twice) and 400x800, Escape and Sift's Close both remove the 'New Message' sheet. Sift then has no To field, no input values and no 'New Message' heading anywhere. The page's compose stays visible with To 'a@b'. Opening an email and going Back to Inbox does not bring it back. Switching Sift off and on does not bring it back either; only the original view shows it. Pressing Compose again empties the page's draft, which is the fixture's own behavior. At 1280x900 the inline form works. It needs a compose box with no close control that COMPOSE_CLOSE matches. Real Gmail in English or Spanish has 'Save & close', so real-world reach is limited, but it matches the standard used to accept F700. Medium on the fixture. Not a regression in the strict sense: it is the outcome the F700 skeptic predicted if only the ref were added.
confirmed.fix: Same as F700: in src/content/adapters/gmail.ts, make floatingCompose() true for a compose box with no COMPOSE_CLOSE control, or decide on backdrop or maximized state instead of the 50% area rule. Composeform() then renders it inline and it is never a dismissable page.dialog. Or have closeDialog() in src/content/index.ts undo the dismissal when there is no closeRef and the page still shows the box after Escape.

Original (Sift off): pageValue 80, counter '0 characters left', the page logs a saved signature of 80 characters. Sift: Sift's textarea has maxLength -1, the page's textarea gets 92 characters, counter '-12 characters left', the page logs 'saved sig' with 92 characters. r4-checkout with document.getElementById('zip').maxLength=5: typing 941031234 in Sift's ZIP field puts '941031234' (9 characters) into the page field. The original stops at 5. Not a regression: no maxlength handling existed before round 7 either.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6 && SIFT_PORT=9466 SIFT_TAB=T6-fixtures bun research/r8t6/maxlen-orig.ts   (prints original vs sift: pageValue 80 vs 92)
confirmed.suspectedCause: Sift renders form fields without copying maxlength (or minlength or pattern) from the page's element. The proxy then sets the page field's value from code, which bypasses maxlength.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on its own tab (skeptic, port 9466). research/r8t6/maxlen-orig.ts types 92 characters. Original: pageValue 80, counter '0 characters left', log [80]. Sift: pageValue 92, counter '-12 characters left', and the page's change handler logged a 92-character signature. On r4-checkout, with maxLength=5 set on #zip, typing 941031234 into Sift's ZIP field put '941031234' into the page field. Sift's field is <input data-ref=r8 ... name=zip> with no maxlength. grep finds no maxlength or minlength anywhere in src/. The value reaches the page past a limit the original enforces, so Sift does not have the same effect as the original. Severity is at least medium.
confirmed.fix: Copy the limit from the page field. Add maxLength to the Field model: model.ts, plus generic.ts around line 1866 where autocomplete/accept/multiple are read (el.maxLength >= 0 ? el.maxLength : undefined). Set maxLength={f.maxLength} in TextField's `common` props in src/content/ui/app.tsx (~line 205). As a backstop, in proxy.ts setValue(), clamp the value to el.maxLength when it is >= 0 for input and textarea elements, as typing would.

confirmed.title: Text the page changes as the user types (a 'N characters left' counter) shows the wrong value for about 2.5 s after each keystroke
confirmed.where: http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r8-settings.html, Signature field and its live counter. src/content/index.ts schedule(): 'if (minor && performance.now() - actedAt > 5000) d = Math.max(d, 2500);'
confirmed.evidence: research/r8t6/counterkey.ts types one key every 150 ms. After the 1st and 2nd keys Sift matched in 4 and 113 ms. From the 3rd key on, each update reached Sift only after 2501-2553 ms. research/r8t6/counterlag.ts types 'Baked with love' at 20 ms/key: in 6 of 6 runs, Sift's counter matched the page 2284-2538 ms after the last key. Until then it read, for example, '67 characters left' while the page said '65'. A screen reader user hears the stale value. By contrast, r7-signup's password checklist (class changes) matched within 2-522 ms of each key. Not a regression: the same line is in sift-r7-base (index.ts:1409).
confirmed.suspectedCause: Typing in a Sift field does not set actedAt, so the page's text-only answer to typing counts as a 'minor' change (like a clock). Each one is delayed to at least 2500 ms.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. counterkey.ts at 150 ms per key: 'R' matched in 7 ms and 'y' in 115 ms. Both were still inside the 3 s load window. 'e' through 'f' matched in 2508-2600 ms each. counterlag.ts as written missed the field in my tab (it does not scroll into view), so I reran it with my own version that checks focus, 3 runs. Focus was in Sift's textarea each time. Sift read '80 characters left' during all typing and for about 2 s after the last key, while the page said '65'. It matched 2029, 2040 and 2114 ms after the last key. The cause matches the code. The page's reply to an input event is a text-only childList mutation, so the mutation observer passes minor=true (index.ts ~2221-2257). Typing goes through H.input/proxy.setValue and never sets actedAt, so schedule() applies the 2500 ms floor (index.ts:1484). Any text-only answer to typing lags the same way, including inline validation text written with textContent. This is a sync defect, not polish.
confirmed.fix: Record a typing time in the input handler that calls proxy.setValue (index.ts ~2966), e.g. typedAt = performance.now(). In schedule(), skip the minor 2500 ms floor when the last typing was within about 2 s: `if (minor && performance.now() - Math.max(actedAt, typedAt) > 5000)`. Keep the floor for clocks.

confirmed.title: Sift's relay of the page's live region glues control names together ('9:009:3010:3014:0016:30')
confirmed.where: http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r8-slots.html, the time list after a day is picked. src/content/index.ts newAlert(): text = el.innerText.replace(/\s+/g,' ')
confirmed.evidence: After a click on 'Tue Nov 3', Sift's only status region (div role=status aria-live=polite) holds '5 free times on Tuesday, November 3 9:009:3010:3014:0016:30'. Thu Nov 5 gives '4 free times on Thursday, November 5 9:0010:3011:0014:00'. The page's aria-live region holds separate buttons (9:00, 9:30, …) with no whitespace between them, as React-built lists usually do. A screen reader reading the page's own region names each button. Sift's text reads as one run-on number.
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-6 && SIFT_PORT=9466 SIFT_TAB=T6-fixtures bun research/r8t6/go.ts goto:http://127.0.0.1:8799/fx/r8-slots.html wait:2500 "click:Tue Nov 3" wait:1800 "eval:[...document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('[role=status]')].map(e=>e.textContent).join('|')"
confirmed.suspectedCause: innerText puts no separator between adjacent inline-block controls. The relay should join the accessible names of the region's child elements (or insert a space between element boundaries) instead.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice. After 'Tue Nov 3' was clicked, Sift's only polite status region held '5 free times on Tuesday, November 3 9:009:3010:3014:0016:30', and the listener recorded the same string as said. The page's own #slots innerText is '...November 3\n\n9:009:3010:3014:0016:30'. newAlert() uses el.innerText.replace(/\s+/g,' '), and innerText puts no separator between adjacent inline-block buttons that have no whitespace between them. While Sift is shown the page is inert, so this relay is all a screen reader hears. The original's region exposes each time as its own button. The run-on string is not a usable list of times. It is at the low end of medium: the first clause ('5 free times...') reads correctly, and the buttons can still be found in Sift's view.
confirmed.fix: In newAlert() in src/content/index.ts, build the text from the region's nodes, not raw innerText. Walk the subtree and join text nodes, adding a separator (', ' or a space) at each element boundary for buttons, links, inline-block elements and elements with roles. Or join the accessible names of interactive descendants. Then collapse whitespace.

confirmed.title: Round 7's looser link-word checks let a link the model moved keep words that name a different action: 'Update your email preferences' unsubscribes, 'cancel your subscription' subscribes
confirmed.evidence: Chrome 9469 with the mock, fixture scratchpad/r8ai/fx/nearswap.html. The source sentence is 'To unsubscribe from all emails, use this link, and to update your email preferences, sign in to your account settings…'. The model text is '[Update your email preferences](L0) in your account settings.' Sift's Short version shows '[link] Update your email preferences', and clicking it fires the page's /unsubscribe link (document.body.dataset.clicked = '/unsubscribe'). Offline (r8ai/t/nearswap.ts), '[Change the delivery address](L0)' opens /orders/cancel when the sentence is 'If you want to cancel your order, click here; to change the delivery address, call…'. Offline (r8ai/t/stem.ts), '[cancel your subscription](L0)' is accepted for the 'Subscribe' link (/subscribe): stemOf matches subscription/subscribe on 7 shared letters. The pre-round-7 sameWords rejected all three, because the words share no exact word of 4 or more letters with the link text, so the link went to 'Links in the full text'. This reopens part of F616: the action does something other than its label says. It depends on the model misplacing a link id, as F616 did.

In Chrome: run r8ai/mock.ts (port 8873, NEARSWAP marker), SIFT_PORT=9469 bun r8ai/settings.ts, then SIFT_PORT=9469 SIFT_TAB=R3-ai-background bun r8ai/outline.ts nearswap.html 5, then bun scripts/act.ts 'click:Update your email preferences' wait:500 'eval:document.body.dataset.clicked'.
confirmed.suspectedCause: nearWords accepts any words that come from the link's whole sentence (12 words before and after, split only at . ! ?), so the words of another clause in that sentence ('to update your email preferences') pass. The two-links guard covers only sentences with two links. stemOf accepts any two words sharing a long prefix, and opposite actions often share one (subscribe/subscription). A fix could take near words only from the link's own clause (stop at ; , and 'and to'), and require a stem match only for words that are not verbs of another action. Otherwise keep the old exact-word rule for the action word.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium. This is a regression from round 7. It depends on the model putting a link id on the wrong clause, as F616 did. In Chrome 9469 with the mock, nearswap.html showed '[link] Update your email preferences' in the Short version. A trusted click on it set document.body.dataset.clicked to '/unsubscribe'. On the original page, that link reads 'use this link' and sits in the 'To unsubscribe from all emails' clause. Offline, nearswap.ts accepted both swaps: 'Change the delivery address' opened /orders/cancel, and 'Update your email preferences' opened /unsubscribe. stem.ts accepted '[cancel your subscription](L0)' for the 'Subscribe' link (/subscribe). I ran the same three tests against the pre-round-7 code in /home/nico/projects/sift-r7-base. There, the first two swaps and the stem case lose the link: the words stay as plain text and the link goes to the extra list. Causes: Link.near holds up to 12 words on each side of the link and stops only at sentence ends (short.ts:160-166), so nearWords (short.ts:389-394) accepts words from another clause of the same sentence. stemOf (short.ts:358-363) matches subscription/subscribe on 7 shared letters. One note: the third offline case ('Download a copy of your data' opening /account/delete) passed in pre-round-7 code too, because sameWords accepted the shared 4-letter word 'your'. That part is older and not a regression.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/short.ts: (1) when building Link.near (around :160-166), cut 'before' and 'after' at clause breaks (; : , and before 'and to', 'or', 'but'), so near words come only from the link's own clause; (2) in sameWords (around :368-376) and nearWords, do not accept a stem-only match for the action word. Require an exact match there, or reject a stem pair when either word is a known opposite or other action verb (cancel/subscribe, delete/download, unsubscribe/update). Also make sameWords skip stopwords like 'your' and 'this' for its 4-letter rule.

confirmed.title: Isolating filtered list entries re-runs the whole three-model chain for every sub-batch and forgets the unsettled entries: 3 filtered headlines in 20 cost 28 calls on the first visit, 28 on the second and 11 on the third
confirmed.where: src/background/index.ts:605-627 (run), :572-591 (each ask goes through withChain with all three models), :476 (MAX_LINE_CALLS)
confirmed.evidence: Chrome 9469 with the mock (a content_filter answer with no text for any batch holding a [FILTER] title). Fixture scratchpad/r8ai/fx/threefilter.html: 20 news headlines, 3 of them flagged. Visit 1 made 28 calls, 24 of them filtered: each filtered sub-batch was tried on mock/lines, then lines-fb, then last, with sizes 20×3, 10×3, 5×3, … Only 9 of the 17 innocent headlines got lines. The other 8, all in the second half, kept their titles on that view, because the 12-ask cap was reached and the rest was 'unsettled'. Visit 2 made 28 more calls (24 filtered), visit 3 made 11 (9 filtered). That is 67 calls for one list of 20, and round 6 made 3. One filtered headline in 6 (onefilter.html) took 15 calls, 12 of them filtered. Once the full batch has been refused by all three models, every sub-batch that still holds the flagged entry is refused by all three again. The cache then keeps a keep-title row (1 day) only for the isolated entries, so the daily expiry starts a new isolation.
confirmed.repro: Run r8ai/mock.ts on 8873 and SIFT_PORT=9469 bun r8ai/settings.ts (clears the cache). Then three times: SIFT_PORT=9469 SIFT_TAB=R3-ai-background bun r8ai/watch.ts threefilter.html 20 zzzz; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8873/log | count the lines entries and filter:true. To see which entries got lines on visit 1: bun scripts/act.ts 'eval:[...document.querySelector("sift-root").shadowRoot.querySelectorAll("a")].map(a=>a.innerText.slice(0,40))'.
confirmed.suspectedCause: run() calls ask() for every half, and ask() always walks [lines, linesFallback, lastResort]. After a chain-wide final refusal, the halves could be isolated on one model, and the fallbacks asked only for the isolated entry. Entries left when MAX_LINE_CALLS is reached are not remembered for this batch, so the next visit starts again from the top. They could be remembered in the session (or in the cache, briefly), or the cap could count HTTP calls rather than asks.
confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium at most. This needs every model in the chain to refuse the batch. In Chrome 9469 with the mock and a cleared cache, threefilter.html made 28 lines calls (24 filtered) on visit 1, 28 (24 filtered) on visit 2 and 11 (9 filtered) on visit 3, the same counts as reported. The visit 1 sequence was 20F x3 models, 10F x3, 5 ok, 5F x3, 3F x3, 2F x3, 1F x3, 1 ok, 1 ok, 2 ok, 10F x3, 5F x3, then the cap. On visit 1, entries 0-4 and 6-9 got lines. Entries 11-15 and 17-19 (8 innocent headlines) kept their titles. onefilter.html took 15 calls (12 filtered), and its revisit made 0 calls. So the restart only happens when the cap is hit. The code matches the claim. In run() (background/index.ts:605-627), each ask() goes through withChain with [lines, linesFallback, lastResort] (:572-575), so MAX_LINE_CALLS = 12 counts asks, not HTTP calls. That allows up to 36 calls per batch, against its comment 'each try may be paid for'. Entries left 'unsettled' at the cap are not remembered, so each visit starts the isolation again. Round 6 (sift-r7-base :581) made one chain walk and cached KEEP_TITLE for all entries. Caveat: with the default chain (Gemini, then GPT-6-luna twice), this needs both providers to filter the same headlines. When only one model is reachable, each ask costs one call, which still means 12 calls per visit.
confirmed.fix: In src/background/index.ts doLines run()/ask(): once a whole batch got a final refusal from every model, isolate the halves on the model that refused first. Ask the fallbacks only for an entry that fails alone. Count HTTP calls toward MAX_LINE_CALLS, not asks. Remember the entries still unsettled at the cap, briefly (in pc or a short cache row), so a revisit does not run the whole isolation again.

Roads north stay closed.' becomes 'Mr. Roads north stay closed.' and 'Dr. Ana Ruiz said…' becomes 'Dr. Roads north stay closed.' confirmed.repro: Run r8ai/mock.ts on 8873 (ABBR marker) and SIFT_PORT=9469 bun r8ai/settings.ts, then SIFT_PORT=9469 SIFT_TAB=R3-ai-background bun r8ai/watch.ts abbrlive.html 4,9,13 'U\.S\.|Roads|Schools'. confirmed.suspectedCause: sentences() ends a sentence at any '.' followed by a space, so 'U.S.' and 'Mr.' become one-token 'sentences'. confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, medium-low. This bug is older than round 7, as claimed. In Chrome 9469 with the mock, abbrlive.html showed 'Roads north stay closed. U.S. officials say the storm killed 12 people. Schools stay shut until Friday.' at 4 s. At 9 s and 13 s, after the lede changed to 31, it showed the new paragraph in full and then 'Roads north stay closed. U.S. Schools stay shut until Friday.' That reads as if U.S. schools are closed. The original page has no such phrase. At 20 s the refresh landed. Offline, abbr2.ts gives 'Mr. Roads north stay closed.' I ran the same test on /home/nico/projects/sift-r7-base and got the same output there. Cause: sentences() (short.ts:458-477) ends a sentence at any '.' followed by a space, so 'U.S.' and 'Mr.' become one-token 'sentences'. The stale test skips them (want.size < 2 in staleAbout) and withoutSentences keeps them, while the sentence they start is dropped. It only happens on the stale-drop path: a paragraph that changed during the visit. It lasts until the refresh, or for good after MAX_REFRESH (4) refreshes (ai.ts:31).
confirmed.fix: In src/content/short.ts sentences(): do not end a sentence after a short abbreviation or initials, such as a capital letter followed by '.', or Mr/Mrs/Ms/Dr/St/Gen/Sen/Rep/No/e.g./i.e. when the next word follows. As a backstop in withoutSentences, when a sentence is dropped, also drop a kept piece of fewer than 2 tokens right before it.
